proposals.title: Boundary-Preserving Domain and Cell-Type Assignment
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on combining spatial transcriptomic expression with precise spatial neighborhood graphs to delineate tissue domains while resolving cell-type specific signals. By integrating quality control, normalization, and differential expression of marker genes, the method uses boundary-preserving clustering to accurately assign both domains and cell types. Evaluation metrics include cluster purity, expression continuity across boundaries, and marker enrichment, ensuring that the approach captures biologically relevant cellular heterogeneity.

proposals.title: Noise-Robust Denoising via Sensitivity-Driven Neighborhood Optimization
proposals.summary: Here, the pipeline emphasizes adaptive smoothing to mitigate technical noise while preserving sharp expression transitions. Sensitivity-driven metrics guide the optimal construction of spatial graphs, balancing denoising with the retention of critical boundaries. The analysis quantitatively compares pre- and post-denoising expression levels, spatial variability measures, and noise reduction efficiency, thereby underpinning the method’s robustness against sparsity and stochastic noise inherent in spatial transcriptomics.

proposals.title: Cross-Section Alignment and Batch Correction for Integrated Analysis
proposals.summary: This analysis addresses technical variability and batch effects across multiple tissue sections. The pipeline integrates rigorous quality control and normalization with advanced batch correction techniques, followed by spatially informed dimensionality reduction. Alignment metrics and registration quality are assessed to ensure precise integration across sections. The outcome is a coherent dataset that allows for reliable cross-comparison of tissue domains and better interpretation of spatial gene expression patterns across specimens.

proposals.title: Three-Dimensional Reconstruction through Serial Section Integration
proposals.summary: Focused on reconstructing the 3D architecture of tissues, this workflow performs spatial registration of serial sections using both expression and spatial coordinates. Sequential integration of multiple sections enables detailed 3D reconstructions, validated by comparing reconstructed spatial continuity and tissue boundaries with known histological landmarks. Metrics such as 3D alignment accuracy and consistency of domain organization across sections confirm the pipeline’s ability to capture complex tissue structures.

proposals.title: Spatial Autocorrelation-Driven Clustering for Domain Characterization
proposals.summary: This pipeline leverages spatial autocorrelation metrics to fine-tune clustering parameters that more accurately reflect the inherent spatial structure. Incorporating both expression levels and local spatial relationships, the method validates clusters using differential expression and spatial continuity analyses. Comparisons focus on how well the clusters recapitulate known tissue architectures while maintaining robust separation between distinct biological domains, enhancing interpretability of spatial patterns.

proposals.title: Optimized Dimensionality Reduction for Joint Expression-Spatial Analysis
proposals.summary: This analysis employs a tailored dimensionality reduction technique that jointly considers high-dimensional gene expression and spatial data. The reduction is optimized to highlight subtle local variations while preserving global tissue structure. Evaluation is based on preservation of spatial gradients, minimization of noise influence, and consistency in recovering known biological domains. The approach provides a low-dimensional embedding that improves subsequent clustering and visual interpretation of tissue organization.

proposals.title: Quantitative Assessment of Denoising Behavior and Noise Robustness
proposals.summary: In this systematic evaluation, the method’s denoising performance is rigorously quantified using predefined noise metrics and sensitivity analyses. The pipeline assesses the impact of different smoothing techniques on both expression signal recovery and spatial coherence. By comparing signal-to-noise ratios, cluster stability, and preservation of sharp boundaries before and after denoising, the approach provides a detailed account of noise robustness, highlighting its suitability for sparse and variable spatial transcriptomics data.

proposals.title: Graph-Based Integration for 3D Tissue Organization Characterization
proposals.summary: This proposal centers on using graph theory to integrate two-dimensional spatial datasets into a coherent three-dimensional tissue model. By constructing optimized spatial neighborhood graphs across sections, the method enables the reconstruction of complex tissue architectures. Validation involves comparing reconstructed 3D structures against expected tissue landmarks and quantitative metrics such as graph connectivity and consistency of domain boundaries, thus offering deep insights into tissue organization and structural heterogeneity.

proposals.title: Multi-Scale Analysis of Tissue Domains from Spot to Cellular Resolution
proposals.summary: Designed to bridge analyses across different spatial scales, this workflow examines how resolution variability influences domain delineation. By performing parallel analyses at the multicellular spot level and near-cellular bead or pixel level, the pipeline contrasts expression patterns and spatial clustering outcomes. Comparative metrics include domain stability across scales, resolution-dependent noise characteristics, and marker gene consistency. This multi-scale approach provides a comprehensive picture of tissue organization while accounting for technical variations in resolution.

plan.user_request: Coordinate agents to propose, critique, and finalize exactly nine computational spatial-omics analyses likely performed in the hidden paper, producing draft, critique, and final proposal JSON files at the specified paths.

steps.title: Draft candidate analysis proposals
steps.description: The Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) reads the PUBLIC BACKGROUND description and writes `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`, containing a structured draft list of nine candidate spatial-omics analyses, each with a tentative title and detailed summary that reflect likely assessments of domain accuracy, denoising behavior, cross-section integration, and three-dimensional organization in spatial transcriptomics data.
steps.reasoning: A focused drafting step, explicitly owned by `spatial_cv_agent`, is needed to turn the textual background into concrete but provisional analysis ideas that can later be critiqued and refined, while ensuring the proposals are grounded in the stated evaluation axes of the hidden paper.
steps.assignment_rationale: This step must be handled by the Spatial-CV Planning Agent by user specification, and it is purpose-built to draft exactly nine spatial analysis proposals into draft_proposals.json using internal draft–critic–revision cycles.

steps.title: Critique the draft proposals
steps.description: The Critic Agent loads `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and produces `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`, giving a structured critique for each of the nine candidate analyses and for the set as a whole, assessing clarity, distinctness, plausibility, redundancy, and coverage of the PUBLIC BACKGROUND themes, without modifying the draft file.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critique step is required to systematically evaluate and document the strengths and weaknesses of the drafted analyses before finalization, so that the subsequent synthesis can correct issues (e.g., overlap or gaps in evaluation criteria) using an explicit, machine-readable critique artifact.
steps.assignment_rationale: This step is a pure critique of the draft proposals and writes only critique.json, which matches the critic_agent’s advertised role as a review-only agent that produces hypotheses/critique.json.

steps.title: Synthesize and finalize proposals
steps.description: A Hypothesis/Synthesis Agent uses both `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` to revise and consolidate the nine analyses into a coherent final set, then writes `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, mapping to an array of exactly nine items, where each item contains only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing one spatial-omics analysis likely performed in the hidden paper.
steps.reasoning: This synthesis step is needed to transform the critiqued drafts into a polished, non-redundant collection of nine final proposals that adhere strictly to the required output schema and fully reflect the evaluation priorities implied by the PUBLIC BACKGROUND, using the critique as guidance while producing the single required final artifact.
steps.assignment_rationale: This step requires final synthesis of exactly nine proposals into final_proposals.json, which aligns with hypothesis_agent’s role as the general-purpose drafting and final-synthesis agent for spatial paper analyses.

provenance.justification: The plan adapts the high-level pattern of the `paper_hypothesis_generation` template—draft → critic review → finalize—to the current task of proposing spatial-omics analyses without involving PDFs or datasets and under the constraint of exactly three steps and three specific artifacts. The template’s notion of draft hypotheses, critic feedback, and revised hypotheses was abstracted to draft proposals, critique, and final proposals, while omitting intermediate inventory and feasibility steps and not using any plan template as a candidate analysis itself.
